_comment: Write guards (spec Sec.10.1). Both entries prefer `python3` and fall back
to `python`, for the reason bin/se-buddy and bin/_bootstrap.py already do:
macOS 12.3+ and modern Debian/Ubuntu ship no `python` at all, only
`python3`. These two commands used to invoke bare `python`, and Claude
Code treats a hook whose interpreter cannot be found as a NON-BLOCKING
error - the tool call proceeds. So on those platforms both guards silently
did not run, and the second of the two write-protection layers this
project advertises did not exist. `se-buddy doctor` now executes a guard
rather than only parsing this file, so that can never be silent again.
POSIX sh, deliberately: hook commands run under `sh` on macOS/Linux and
Git Bash on Windows, and no bashism is needed here. `exec` matters - it
replaces the shell so the script's exit 2 reaches Claude Code as the
block, rather than the shell's own exit status.
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is expanded by Claude Code before the shell sees it;
the quotes are what survive a plugin root containing spaces.

hooks.command: if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block_capella_write.py"; else exec python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block_capella_write.py"; fi
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block_write_verbs.py"; else exec python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block_write_verbs.py"; fi
